speakers: Mormon, speaking in his own voice
principles: The obedience of the earth against the resistance of men
Repentance declared so men might be saved

world_behind.title: The chapter has no events
world_behind.text: Mormon leaves the narrative after Helaman 11:38 and does not return to it until Helaman 13. Every verse is comment.

world_behind.title: It is written about the cycle just shown
world_behind.text: Helaman 11 ran war, famine, repentance, prosperity, forgetting, and ripening in one chapter, and verses 1 through 3 name that pattern.

world_behind.title: The list of blessings comes first
world_behind.text: Verse 2 counts out crops, cattle, precious metal, rescue, and enemies turned mild before saying what the people did with them.

world_behind.title: Verse 15 states a physical claim
world_behind.text: Mormon says it is the earth that moves and not the sun, in a book that elsewhere speaks of the sun standing still.

world_behind.title: The chapter turns on obedience
world_behind.text: Verses 8 through 21 list things that obey God's voice, and men are the exception the whole list is built around.

world_behind.title: The cursing of hidden treasure is introduced here
world_behind.text: Verses 18 and 19 state it as a principle, and Helaman 13:18 will have Samuel prophesy it over the land.

world_behind.title: The close is a quotation
world_behind.text: Verse 26 ends by fulfilling words about everlasting life and everlasting damnation, in the language of John 5:29.

words.text: Instability, failure to hold a course. The word occurs once in all of scripture, here, as the first thing Mormon says about the human heart.
Treated at 2 Nephi 28:24, in the wo pronounced on those at ease in Zion. Verse 2 names it with great prosperity as the pair of conditions under which the hardening happened.
Treated at 1 Nephi 16:25, of the Lord chastening Lehi. The record uses the word eight times. Verse 3 makes chastening the condition under which the people remember at all.
The state of being nothing. The record uses the word three times, twice in Benjamin's sermon at Mosiah 4 and once here. Verse 7 measures it against the dust of the earth.
Placed under a curse. The record uses the word six times, three of them in this chapter at verses 18, 19, and 20. Two are about buried treasure and one is about a man.
Condemnation, the state of the finally lost. The record uses the word ten times and the King James Bible eleven, including John 5:29, which verse 26 quotes almost exactly.

phrases.term: How false, and also the unsteadiness of the hearts of the children of men
phrases.text: The thesis, given before any argument. The second half of the same verse says God blesses and prospers those who trust him.

phrases.term: Then is the time that they do harden their hearts
phrases.text: The hinge of the long sentence. Everything before it is a list of blessings, and this clause says when the trouble started.

phrases.term: This because of their ease, and their exceedingly great prosperity
phrases.text: The cause named at the end of the verse. Not defeat, not oppression, and not persecution.

phrases.term: Except the Lord doth chasten his people with many afflictions... they will not remember him
phrases.text: The rule Helaman 11 had just demonstrated twice. Mormon states it without softening the claim.

phrases.term: How quick to do iniquity, and how slow to do good
phrases.text: The pairing that runs through verses 4 and 5. Quick to hearken to the evil one, quick to be lifted up, quick to boast, and slow to remember.

phrases.term: They will not that he should be their guide
phrases.text: The refusal put at its simplest. Verse 6 says they do set his counsels at naught despite his goodness and mercy.

phrases.term: O how great is the nothingness of the children of men; yea, even they are less than the dust of the earth
phrases.text: The comparison the next fourteen verses justify. Dust obeys, and the argument is built on that.

phrases.term: Surely it is the earth that moveth and not the sun
phrases.text: An aside about astronomy inside a sermon about obedience. Mormon states it as a correction to the way the day would look.

phrases.term: If a man hide up a treasure in the earth
phrases.text: The principle stated before it becomes a prophecy. Helaman 13:18 will apply it to the whole land.

phrases.term: For this cause, that men might be saved, hath repentance been declared
phrases.text: The purpose clause that turns the chapter. Everything before it is the problem, and this sentence gives the provision.

phrases.term: Restored unto grace for grace, according to their works
phrases.text: Mormon's phrase for the outcome he hopes for. Grace and works appear in the same clause without tension.

verses.label: v. 1–3
verses.title: A chapter that is all aside and no story
verses.text: The abridger's formula opens three consecutive verses and nothing narrative follows any of them: "thus we can behold how false, and also the unsteadiness of the hearts of the children of men" (v. 1), "we may see at the very time when he doth prosper his people" (v. 2), "thus we see that except the Lord doth chasten his people with many afflictions... they will not remember him" (v. 3). Elsewhere in the volume the phrase closes an episode. Here there is no episode. Twenty-six verses of comment stand between the end of Helaman 11 and the resumption of the account in Helaman 13.

verses.label: v. 4–5
verses.title: One pair of adverbs carrying the whole indictment
verses.text: The complaint is built from a contrast repeated four times in two verses: "how quick to do iniquity, and how slow to do good"; "how quick to be lifted up in pride; yea, how quick to boast"; "how slow are they to remember the Lord their God." Quick stands four times in these two verses and nowhere else in the chapter. Nothing specific is charged. The accusation is entirely about the speed at which two kinds of action are taken.

verses.label: v. 7–8
verses.title: A comparison whose grounds are obedience, not size
verses.text: Verse 7 makes the claim, "O how great is the nothingness of the children of men; yea, even they are less than the dust of the earth." Verse 8 supplies the reason, and it is not about how small people are: "the dust of the earth moveth hither and thither, to the dividing asunder, at the command of our great and everlasting God." Dust is greater because it does as it is told. The argument depends on the previous verses having established that men do not, and the record makes the connection by placing the two verses side by side without a connective.

verses.label: v. 9–17
verses.title: Nine verses of one grammatical form
verses.text: The chapter turns into a catalogue of conditionals, each stating a command and its immediate execution. "If he say unto the earth, Move, it is moved" (v. 13). "If he say unto the waters of the great deep, Be thou dried up, it is done" (v. 16). "If he say unto this mountain, Be thou raised up, and come over and fall upon that city, that it be buried up, behold it is done" (v. 17). The sentence pattern does not vary across nine verses, and the record never supplies an instance of any of them happening.

verses.label: v. 14–15
verses.title: An appearance distinguished from a mechanism
verses.text: One item in the catalogue gets a gloss the others do not: "if he say unto the earth, Thou shalt go back, that it lengthen out the day for many hours, it is done." Verse 15 then explains what an observer would see and corrects it: "the earth goeth back, and it appeareth unto man that the sun standeth still; yea, and behold, this is so; for surely it is the earth that moveth and not the sun." The event described is the one at Joshua 10:13, where the sun is said to have stood still. The record keeps the event and states that the description of it is a description of how it looked.

verses.label: v. 25
verses.title: A wish stated, and then overruled by a text
verses.text: The writer puts his own desire on the page and immediately sets a limit against it: "I would that all men might be saved. But we read that in the great and last day there are some who shall be cast out, yea, who shall be cast off from the presence of the Lord." The word but does the work, and the authority invoked is not a revelation to him but something read. A chapter that has spent seventeen verses on what God can do ends by reporting what the writer cannot have.

chapter.title: The dangerous condition is prosperity
chapter.text: Verse 2 lists eight blessings and then says that was when they hardened. The chapter treats comfort as the risk that persecution is usually assumed to be.

chapter.title: Affliction is presented as the only reliable teacher
chapter.text: Verse 3 says without chastening they will not remember. Mormon does not qualify it, and Helaman 11 is his evidence.

chapter.title: Quick and slow are the terms of the indictment
chapter.text: Verses 4 and 5 describe a speed problem rather than an ignorance problem. They know what is right and are slow at it.

chapter.title: The argument runs through obedience
chapter.text: Dust, hills, mountains, the earth, the day, the deep, and buried treasure all obey a voice. Human beings are the item on the list that does not.

chapter.title: Mormon corrects the appearance of the sky
chapter.text: Verse 15 says the earth moves and the sun does not, in a passage about a lengthened day.

chapter.title: The chapter's mood changes at verse 22
chapter.text: Twenty-one verses of indictment turn on the word "therefore," and the reason given is that men might be saved.

chapter.title: Grace and works stand together
chapter.text: Verse 24 asks for repentance, good works, and restoration to grace for grace, in one sentence with no seam.

chapter.title: He states his own wish and then the doctrine
chapter.text: Verse 25 has "I would that all men might be saved" followed immediately by what the record says will happen. The wish is preserved and not allowed to settle the question.

applications.title: Measure yourself against something that does not move
applications.text: The verse sets the unsteadiness of human hearts beside a goodness that keeps blessing regardless. When you are judging how you are doing, pick a fixed reference rather than comparing this week to last week.

applications.title: Set a guard on the good years
applications.text: The hardening happened during the increase, not during the loss. Whatever practice keeps you honest should get stricter when things go well.

applications.title: Ask whether you are slow rather than ignorant
applications.text: The charge is quickness in one direction and slowness in the other. Speed of response is a thing you can measure in yourself.

applications.title: Watch what you are refusing to be guided by
applications.text: They set his counsels at naught while acknowledging his goodness. Rejecting guidance rarely looks like denying its source.

applications.title: Let the size of things put you in scale
applications.text: Mormon uses dust, mountains, and the deep to locate a person. Perspective of that kind tends to make people steadier rather than smaller.

applications.title: Correct your own illustration
applications.text: Mormon stops to note that the sun only appears to stand still, since it is the earth that moves. When you know a detail your own example glosses over, put it in, because a reader who spots it later trusts everything else less.

applications.title: Ask what the power is for
applications.text: After a long stretch on what God's voice can do, the reason given for declaring repentance is that men might be saved. When a description of capability has run long, look for the sentence that says what it serves.

applications.title: Keep the wish and the report apart
applications.text: Mormon writes that he would have all men saved, and then states what he reads instead. Wanting something and reporting something are different acts, and separating them on the page is what makes both of them credible.

questions.text: What has gone well for me lately, and what has it done to me?
What has actually made me remember God?
What am I quick to do that I wish I were slow at?
Whose counsel do I set at naught while praising them?
When did I last feel my own scale honestly?
What have I hidden up that I would not want cursed?
What is repentance for, in my own words?
